questions.q: What will the father’s commands and teachings add to his son?
questions.a: The father’s commands and teachings will add years of life and peace to his son.

questions.q: Where must covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness be written?
questions.a: Covenant faithfulness and trustworthiness must be written on the tablet of one’s heart.

questions.q: On what must the son not lean?
questions.a: The son must not lean on (rely on) his own understanding.

questions.q: How must the son not see himself?
questions.a: The son must not see himself as wise.

questions.q: What must the son do with his wealth?
questions.a: The son must honor Yahweh with his wealth.
Yahweh disciplines those whom he loves.

questions.q: What benefits people more than having silver or gold?
questions.a: Being wise benefits people more than silver could benefit them. Indeed, being wise is worth more to people than having gold.

questions.q: What are all the paths of wisdom?
questions.a: All the paths of wisdom are peace.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do by being wise?
questions.a: Yahweh made the world through being wise.

questions.q: What will be life to the son’s soul?
questions.a: Prudence and discretion will be life to the son’s soul.

questions.q: If the son walks in wisdom, what will happen when he lies down?
questions.a: When he lies down, he will not fear anything, and he will sleep peacefully.

questions.q: Of what should the son not be afraid?
questions.a: The son should not be afraid of sudden dread or devastation.

questions.q: What should the son do for those who deserve it?
questions.a: The son should not withhold what is good from people who deserve it.

questions.q: What should the son not do to his neighbor?
questions.a: The son should not make a plan to harm his neighbor.
Yahweh detests people who act wickedly.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do to the mockers?

commentary.text: To piety, and to improve afflictions.

Verses 1–6 In the way of believing obedience to God's commandments health and peace may commonly be enjoyed; and though our days may not be long upon earth, we shall live for ever in heaven. Let not mercy and truth forsake thee; God's mercy in promising, and his truth in performing: live up to them, keep up thine interest in them, and take the comfort of them. We must trust in the Lord with all our hearts, believing he is able and wise to do what is best. Those who know themselves, find their own understandings a broken reed, which, if they lean upon, will fail. Do not design any thing but what is lawful, and beg God to direct thee in every case, though it may seem quite plain. In all our ways that prove pleasant, in which we gain our point, we must acknowledge God with thankfulness. In all our ways that prove uncomfortable, and that are hedged up with thorns, we must acknowledge him with submission. It is promised, He shall direct thy paths; so that thy way shall be safe and good, and happy at last.

There is not a greater enemy to the fear of the Lord in the heart, than self-conceit of our own wisdom. The prudence and sobriety which religion teaches, tend not only to the health of the soul, but to the health of the body. Worldly wealth is but poor substance, yet, such as it is, we must honour God with it; and those that do good with what they have, shall have more to do more good with. Should the Lord visit us with trials and sickness, let us not forget that the exhortation speaks to us as to children, for our good. We must not faint under an affliction, be it ever so heavy and long, not be driven to despair, or use wrong means for relief. The father corrects the son whom he loves, because he loves him, and desires that he may be wise and good. Afflictions are so far from doing God's children any hurt, that, by the grace of God, they promote their holiness.

No precious jewels or earthly treasures are worthy to be compared with true wisdom, whether the concerns of time or eternity be considered. We must make wisdom our business; we must venture all in it, and be willing to part with all for it. This Wisdom is the Lord Jesus Christ and his salvation, sought and obtained by faith and prayer. Were it not for unbelief, remaining sinfulness, and carelessness, we should find all our ways pleasantness, and our paths peace, for his are so; but we too often step aside from them, to our own hurt and grief. Christ is that Wisdom, by whom the worlds were made, and still are in being; happy are those to whom he is made of God wisdom. He has wherewithal to make good all his promises.

Let us not suffer Christ's words to depart from us, but keep sound wisdom and discretion; then shall we walk safely in his ways. The natural life, and all that belongs to it, shall be under the protection of God's providence; the spiritual life, and all its interests, under the protection of his grace, so that we shall be kept from falling into sin or trouble.

Our business is to observe the precepts of Christ, and to copy his example; to do justice, to love mercy, and to beware of covetousness; to be ready for every good work, avoiding needless strife, and bearing evils, if possible, rather than seeking redress by law. It will be found there is little got by striving. Let us not envy prosperous oppressors; far be it from the disciples of Christ to choose any of their ways. These truths may be despised by the covetous and luxurious, but everlasting contempt will be the portion of such scorners, while Divine favour is shown to the humble believer.
